- If sentiment shows strong negative or positive bias (e.g., -1.00 or 1.00) in recent days, model should adjust forecast downward/upward by 2–5% to counteract sentiment-driven overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overestimate continuation; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a peak), model should not assume trend continuation; apply downward bias in forecast for 3–7 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model should avoid over-optimistic trends; cap forecast growth at 1–2% per day unless confirmed by data.  
- If model forecast is consistently >10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next horizon to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 entries, model should not assume sustained upward trend; introduce early correction if price deviates >3% from 14-day moving average.
